_comment: Canonical taskId -> orchestrator-file mapping. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH, read by both the human-readable dict in SKILL.md and the Step 1.A registration verification snippet. v2.14.27+ uses bare taskIds (no cr- prefix) so Cowork's sidebar renders cleanly. cleanup/reconcile-sent are intentionally ABSENT — they are silent background tasks, not chat orchestrators, and register separately (Step 1.D). pulse maps to orchestrator-dont-forget.md (filename kept for events.jsonl source_skill back-compat; see source_skill_compat.py). CTS1: `commitments` is RETIRED (disabled via the Phase 1 migration table, v2.14.27 pattern) and split into waiting-on + my-plate; waiting-on maps to orchestrator-commitments.md (filename kept for source_skill back-compat, same as pulse).
_retired: `pulse` is RETIRED (SPEC LIFECYCLE1, 2026-08-02) — never register it. Its row stays below ONLY so a workspace that registered the chat before the retirement still resolves its bootloader; the file it names is a retirement stub. Membership test: schedule_config.RETIRED_TASKS.
_renamed: `past-meetings` is RENAMED to `end-of-day` (SPEC EOD2, 2026-08-16), NOT eliminated — the two rows below deliberately name the SAME FILE and that is the mechanism, not an oversight. The registered prompt bakes the orchestrator FILENAME in at registration time (Step 1.B substitutes <ORCHESTRATOR_FILENAME>), so every live `past-meetings` bootloader on the fleet already names orchestrator-past-meetings.md; renaming the file would break every one of them at the next fire, and pointing the new id at a different file would fork the pack in two. One file, two ids, one pack — forever. Nothing here is a stub. Register `end-of-day` on fresh installs; NEVER auto-register it over a still-registered `past-meetings` (schedule_config.registration_target_set is the fence) — that switch is PROPOSED once and taken by the customer.
_readiness_retired: `commitment-triage`, `balance` and `pipeline-digest` are RETIRED (SPEC TASKRET1, M's ruling 2026-08-17) — never register them, never offer them. They are the READINESS class: the product shipped them before the substrate that makes them say anything true existed, so the update bridge DISABLES a live registration rather than proposing the removal, and narrates it. Their rows stay below ONLY so a workspace that registered one before the retirement still resolves its bootloader between the release and the update reaching it; the files they name are retirement stubs. Membership test: schedule_config.RETIRED_TASKS; class test: schedule_config.retirement_class. Each stub carries the literal `OUTPUT CONTRACT` inside its first 2000 bytes — the bootloader's Step 2 grep window — because a stub without it aborts the fire with a false 'plugin corrupted, reinstall' message (BUG-9517; the pulse and upcoming-meetings stubs above WERE the two shipped instances and were fixed by SPEC_RETIREGATE1, which also taught the bootloader to short-circuit a retired id before that grep ever runs). Every row in this map is now walked against both windows by `tests/run_taskret1_test.py` section [C], so a bare file cannot enter here again. The ON-DEMAND skills of the same names are untouched and fully live.
